clips.text: The work of the Neighborhood House settle rnent, at 470 N street southwest, is illustrated in this window display today in the Transportation Building, 829 Seventeenth street, held for the drive to raise funds for its work.
… which will be served in connection with the sale of fancy ar ticles. which is being held through this week at 819 Seventeenth street for the benefit of Neighborhood House.

Progress toward raising a budget of $25,000 for the Neighborhood House at 470 N r street sou hwest, to defray expenses dur.ng the coming year, was reported by Mrs. Charles Denby, assistant financial secretary, at the headquarters for the drive.

“This is particularly true,” she said, "in Southwest Washington, where five staff nurses are regularly on duty, and in Anacostia, where the number of patients carried is sufficient to keep four nurses busy and only two are available.

note: Clips are machine-read text (OCR) from scanned Evening Star pages on the Library of Congress's Chronicling America, lightly cleaned (line-break hyphens rejoined, stray symbols removed); misspellings are the scanner's. Newspapers this old are public domain. Each clip links to its page at loc.gov. Clips that mention race, covenants, deed restrictions or slurs are skipped automatically (keyword list: race, races, racial, colored, coloured, negro, negroes, white only, whites only, for whites, white people, white persons, white residents, caucasian, segregation, segregated, covenant, covenants, restricted, restriction, restrictions, plus a list of slurs), because they need an editor's context; legal notices and lists of private individuals are skipped too.
